note: The main banks were taken as Hungary's three largest by assets, a choice from general knowledge (no central bank or association ranking was read in this pass): OTP Bank, MBH Bank and K&H Bank. OTP Bank: its notice on its credit cards for contracts from 17 July 2017 (in force from 15 October 2026), read 2026-10-30. Of its cards, the Mastercard Bonus and Mastercard BonusGold are on open sale; the classic Mastercard, VISA and Mastercard Arany ended sale on 1 January 2021 and the Otthon card is offered only to borrowers of an OTP mortgage, so none of these is written. For contracts made from 15 October 2026, purchases carried bear 2.78% a month on the Bonus and 2.59% on the BonusGold, and cash 4.15% and 4.16%. The Bonus costs 6,862 forints a year for the main card; the BonusGold 27,760 from its second year (14,232 in the first, introductory and not written) and 3,673 to make the card. The first year's fee refunded on purchases matching it within 45 days is introductory and not written. A cash withdrawal at OTP's own ATMs and branches costs 2.85%, at least 2,276 forints (outside the euro area 3,284 plus 1.72%, not written). The minimum payment is 5% of the credit used, at least 5,000 forints; the late fee and the over-limit fee are 7,388 forints each time; the monthly default interest of 3.771% for contracts from 1 May 2015 is written as the penalty rate. The notice's 15-day period to pay after the statement closes isn't a stated interest-free period, so no grace is written. The notice states no foreign-currency fee. K&H's and MBH Bank's card pages refused the request (403) and weren't read; UniCredit's notice answered with an IP check.
